title: Asian Side of Istanbul: Kadıköy, Moda, Kuzguncuk & Üsküdar
seoTitle: Asian Side of Istanbul Guide: Kadıköy, Moda & Üsküdar
metaDescription: Plan a full day on Istanbul's Asian side: ₺65 ferries to Kadıköy Market and Moda, Üsküdar sunset views, Kuzguncuk streets, and Beylerbeyi Palace.
quickAnswer: Cross to Istanbul's Asian side by 20-minute Şehir Hatları ferry from Karaköy, Eminönü, or Beşiktaş for ₺65.21 on an Istanbulkart. Spend your morning in Kadıköy Market and Moda's waterfront parks, ride north to Beylerbeyi Palace (800 TL, closed Mondays) and Kuzguncuk's wooden lanes, and finish with sunset facing Maiden's Tower in Üsküdar.

body.text: How do you cross to the Asian side by ferry?

Take a municipal [Şehir Hatları ferry](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables/domestic-trips) from Karaköy, Eminönü, or Beşiktaş directly to Kadıköy or Üsküdar. Boats depart every 15 to 20 minutes from early morning until late evening, take 15 to 25 minutes across the Bosphorus, and cost ₺65.21 per ride with an Istanbulkart ([Şehir Hatları Price List](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/price-list)).

Skip bridge taxis during daytime—ferries dodge road gridlock and double as a mini [Bosphorus cruise](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/bosphorus-cruise-istanbul). In storms, the undersea Marmaray links Sirkeci to Üsküdar in four minutes.
What makes Kadıköy Market and Moda worth a full day?

Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) and neighbouring Moda offer Istanbul's sharpest concentration of everyday culinary craft without Sultanahmet's tourist markups. Within ten flat blocks of the ferry pier, you move from fishmongers, pickle shops, and Anatolian regional stews to specialty coffee roasters and seaside walking paths.

Arrive hungry at 10:00. Graze through Güneşli Bahçe Sokak for olives, cheeses, and simit, eat early lunch at an Anatolian esnaf lokantası, then ride or walk the T3 tram loop into Moda for bookshops and Marmara Sea parks.

items: Morning (10:00–13:00): Browse Kadıköy Fish Market, taste pickles (turşu), and eat a seasonal Anatolian lunch.
Early Afternoon (13:00–15:30): Walk Moda's side streets to Moda Coastal Park and historic Moda Pier for tea.
Staying over: Compare Kadıköy against European-side bases in our [where to stay in Istanbul guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/where-to-stay-in-istanbul).

body.text: Where are the best sunset views in Üsküdar?

The Salacak waterfront promenade in Üsküdar delivers Istanbul's clearest sunset view, framing Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) in the foreground with Topkapı Palace, Hagia Sophia, and Süleymaniye Mosque silhouetted across the water. Arrive 40 minutes before sunset to claim a step or tea-garden table.

Unlike European rooftops with steep drink minimums, Salacak stays relaxed and inexpensive. Grab a ₺40 black tea by the stone steps or walk five minutes north to Şemsi Paşa Mosque, a 16th-century Mimar Sinan jewel on the seawall. Üsküdar is conservative and rarely serves alcohol along the promenade, so save wine or rakı for Moda or Kuzguncuk.
How do you combine Kuzguncuk and Beylerbeyi Palace?

Pair Beylerbeyi Palace and Kuzguncuk in a single three-hour northbound loop from Üsküdar Pier using bus 15 (or a ten-minute taxi) along the coastal road. Visit Beylerbeyi Palace first before last admission, then walk or hop one stop south back into Kuzguncuk for late-afternoon coffee.

Built in the 1860s under Sultan Abdülaziz, [Beylerbeyi Palace](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/4/Beylerbeyi-Sarayi) is quieter than Dolmabahçe and takes an hour to tour. Foreign entry is 800 TL (100 TL gardens only), open Tuesday–Sunday 09:00–17:30 (last entry 17:00), closed Mondays ([Beylerbeyi Info](https://topkapi-palace.com/beylerbeyi-palace/)). Five minutes south, Kuzguncuk pairs pastel wooden houses and community gardens (Kuzguncuk Bostanı) with a mosque, church, and synagogue standing blocks apart. Flying via SAW? Combine this day with our [IST vs SAW airport transfer guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/istanbul-airport-transfer).

faq.q: Can I visit Kadıköy, Kuzguncuk, Beylerbeyi Palace, and Üsküdar in one day?
faq.a: Yes, if you start at 09:30 and avoid Mondays when Beylerbeyi Palace is closed. Spend the morning in Kadıköy and Moda, ride north to Beylerbeyi by 14:30, stroll Kuzguncuk at 16:00, and reach Üsküdar's Salacak promenade before sunset.

faq.q: Is the Asian side of Istanbul cheaper than the European side?
faq.a: Generally yes. Neighbourhood cafes, Anatolian lunches, pastries, and boutique hotels in Kadıköy and Üsküdar typically run 15 to 30 percent lower than comparable spots in Sultanahmet, Karaköy, or Nişantaşı, with higher everyday food quality and less tourist pressure.

faq.q: How do I get from Kadıköy to Üsküdar without taking a taxi?
faq.a: Take the Marmaray commuter rail one stop from Ayrılık Çeşmesi to Üsküdar, or ride the direct Şehir Hatları Üsküdar–Kadıköy ferry (₺62.70) or municipal bus 12 along the coast. The rail link takes under ten minutes total.

faq.q: Is Beylerbeyi Palace included in MuseumPass Istanbul?
faq.a: No. Beylerbeyi Palace is managed by Milli Saraylar and excluded from the Ministry of Culture's MuseumPass Istanbul. You buy the 800 TL foreign visitor ticket directly at the palace gate—card payments are accepted and queues are rarely longer than ten minutes.

faq.q: Can you go inside Maiden's Tower from Üsküdar?
faq.a: Yes, small shuttle boats cross from the Salacak pier to Maiden's Tower during daytime museum hours for an additional ticket fee. However, most locals agree the tower looks far more striking viewed from the Üsküdar shoreline at sunset than from inside.

faq.q: Is the Asian side worth visiting in winter?
faq.a: Absolutely. Heated ferry salons, steamy lokanta stews in Kadıköy Market, and quiet weekday rooms inside Beylerbeyi Palace make the Asian side one of Istanbul's strongest cold-weather days—especially paired with tips from our [Türkiye winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide).
